title: Fennec Healthcare integration kickoff - raw jot
body:
Meeting: Fennec Healthcare - Integration kickoff (6/4/2025)
Attendees: Fennec: Claire Ito (CTO), Raj Malhotra (Platform), Benji Ortiz (Security); Redwood: Maya Chen (SE lead), Omar (solutions), Priya (sre), Jonah (infra)

Quick summary:
- Fennec is a mid-size telehealth provider (EMR: MedFlow 3.1) looking to pilot an assistant to summarize visit notes and produce insurance-friendly synopses. They need PHI-safe inference in region and auditability.
- Pilot target: Q3 (start mid-July) with ~500 DAU, peak concurrency ~40 reqs/min, avg request size 600 tokens, occasional longer context (up to ~2k tokens when including visit history).
- Preferred topology: Private deployment (VPC) with option to evaluate Dedicated later. Regulatory req: UK & EU patient data must remain in EU region; US patient data in us-west.

Technical requirements (explicit):
- Data residency: model inference must run in customer VPC in eu-west-1 for EU patients and us-west-2 for US patients.
- KMS/HSM integration: Fennec uses AWS KMS with custom key policy; they want Redwood Private to integrate with their KMS for model encryption and audit logs.
- Network: VPC peering (no public ingress); outbound to Redwood control plane limited to 443 to a small allowlist.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 200ms for short summaries (<= 256 tokens output) and p95 <= 1.2s for longer syntheses (>= 1k tokens), with graceful fallback to a smaller model if SLO breach predicted.
- Auditability: token-level cost logs and request-response hashes stored for 90 days; secure storage (encrypted-at-rest) and ability to export for compliance.
- PHI Redaction: pre-inference redaction pipeline that can mask identifiers (SSN, MRN, phone, email). They want config to toggle redaction strictness per environment.
- Throughput: expected burst to 80 reqs/min during morning triage windows; autoscaling grace period must be tuned so KV cache warm-up doesn’t cause high latencies.

Integration points / data flow (rough):
1) MedFlow webhook -> internal preprocessing lambda (de-IDENTIFY optionally) -> Redwood Private endpoint in VPC -> model -> post-processing (format to insurer schema) -> SFTP batch to insurer gateway or API call.
2) For QA: nightly export of 2k anonymized records to S3 (controlled) for evaluation and quality monitoring.

Gotchas / concerns raised on call (notes to self):
- KV cache warm-up: with per-patient prefixes, cache fragmentation could blow metric targets. Need to propose prefix caching heuristics (e.g., only cache last 3 visits or only cache stable templates).
- Quantization trade-offs: Fennec insists on low-cost inference but worried about hallucination risk after aggressive quant. Suggest A/B on quant profiles and regen-check on clinical phrases.
- Network egress policy: their security team balked at control-plane callbacks; need exact IPs + cert pinning. Sandbox test will require a spare CIDR for us.
- Audit retention: legal asked for 7 years for some records; ops wants to limit token-level logs to 90 days and store hashes beyond that — propose hash+salt approach for long-term compliance.
- Model fine-tuning: they asked about on-prem fine-tuning with their labeled data. Private supports model variants, but fine-tuning pipeline is productized only under an enterprise add-on. Flag for sales.

Prompt & output examples (raw scribbles):
- Input (visit notes): "Pt c/o sore throat, 2 days. PMH: T2DM, HTN. Vitals stable. Rx: amoxicillin 500mg tid x7" -> Desired assistant: 3-sentence patient summary + bulleted follow-ups for PCP + insurance-coded summary (ICD suggestions).
- Safety rule: Never expose raw identifiers in assistant output. If uncertain, output: "Details available in secure chart; contact care team."

Proposed deployment options to present (trade-offs):
- Private (VPC) on customer infra: full isolation, best for compliance, higher onboarding. Need SRE runbook for autoscaling, patching, and KMS setup.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed in customer region): faster onboarding, some isolation, shared control-plane. Could be an intermediate pilot if VPC peering timeline slips.

Action items (owner — due):
- Maya: produce a preliminary runbook draft for VPC peering + KMS steps and required firewall rules (due: 2025-06-10).
- Omar: estimate SKU/cost for sustained 500 DAU and burst profile (include quantized vs fp16) and prepare two pricing scenarios (due: 2025-06-13).
- Priya: draft autoscaling parameters and cache warm-up mitigation options; simulate 2x burst tests (due: 2025-06-12).
- Fennec (Claire): confirm legal retention requirement (7yr vs 90d) and share redaction policy doc (due: 2025-06-09).
- Jonah: spin an internal sandbox cluster in eu-west-1 and provision temporary test keys (due: 2025-06-11).

Outstanding questions to resolve before pilot:
- Can their KMS key policy allow Redwood Private components to call decrypt for model loading, or do we need separate encryption layers?
- For EU residency, do they permit backups to cross-region for DR? (they indicated no) — confirm.
- What patient sampling rate for nightly S3 export is allowed for QA? need concrete limits.

Notes-to-self (quick):
- Keep prompts conservative; enforce extraction-first then synthesis second to limit hallucinations.
- Plan to offer a short evaluation harness: 500 synthetic visits + 100 labeled checks to measure clinical-phrase recall and hallucination rate.
- Tie quality alerts in Redwood Optimize to a small set of golden prompts Claire will provide.

Meeting follow-up: send a one-pager with: topology options, dataflow diagram (ascii), initial cost ballpark, and minimal config checklist for security. Attach a sample prompt set and redaction examples.

Rough sketch ascii dataflow for one-pager:
MedFlow -> (preproc/redact) -> VPC endpoint (Private) -> Model pool (eu-west/us-west) -> postproc -> insurer/SFTP

End of jot. This is raw — prune and turn into tidy call summary for customer email after Omar's cost numbers land.
